explanation_excerpt: hooks/hooks.json at the project root is the canonical, physical source for hook definitions — .claude-plugin/hooks is only a directory symlink pointing at ../hooks, so editing it directly is a no-op tra

gaps.description: Factual error: calling a direct edit of .claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json a 'no-op trap' is wrong. It is a directory symlink, so writes through it DO reach the real file — the corpus's concern is CI integrity/consistency, not that edits vanish.
Missing that .claude-plugin/ also symlinks skills/ and agents/ (not just hooks/), and omits that CI validates the hooks symlink integrity on every PR.

transfer_problems: A contributor runs npm run validate before opening a PR for a brand-new skill and it reports 0 errors. They conclude the skill is ready to submit. Using the corpus's distinction between npm run validate and npm run validate:strict, explain why this conclusion is wrong and what could still be missing.

A teammate is auditing the .claude-plugin/ directory and, seeing that skills/, agents/, and hooks/ are all symlinks, proposes deleting .claude-plugin/ entirely to 'simplify' the repo. Using the corpus's description of the dual-format distribution model, explain what functionality would break and why the symlinks are load-bearing.
